title: Alloco, Fried Plantain
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: Plantain peeled and cut into rounds 1/2 to 1 cm thick, fried in a litre of oil, stirred now and then until a good brown — and tasted: if it is tender inside, it is done.
longDesc: Two printed cues make this the most testable recipe in the street set: ‘the plantain must take on a good brown colour’ and ‘taste it: if it is tender inside, it is cooked’. 1.5 kg of plantain is peeled and cut into fairly thick rounds, 1/2 to 1 cm; a litre of palm, peanut or sunflower oil is heated in a deep fryer or pot; the rounds are fried, stirred from time to time so the slices colour evenly. No temperature is printed. The page does not frame the dish as specifically Senegalese — alloco is a pan-West-African street food.
ingredients: 1 litre palm, peanut or sunflower oil
steps: In a fryer or heavy pot, heat the litre of oil.
Meanwhile, peel the plantains and cut them into fairly thick rounds, 1/2 to 1 cm.
Fry, stirring from time to time so the slices colour evenly, until the plantain takes on a good brown colour.
Taste one: if it is tender inside, it is done. Drain and serve hot.
chefTips: Two printed cues: the brown colour and the tenderness when tasted.
No temperature is printed; keep the heat moderate so the inside cooks before the outside burns.
Ripeness is not stated — the recipe does not say yellow or black plantain.
commonMistakes: Frying cold, which soaks up oil.
Pulling them when brown but still firm inside — taste, as the page says.
healthBenefits: Plantain provides potassium and slow-release carbohydrate.
culturalNote: Savoura frames the dish simply as ‘Alloco’, a fried plantain; the research notes that Afrik does not present it as specifically Senegalese. It is street food across West Africa.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Alloco’. Byline: Amina Savoura. Publication: Afrik (afrik.com). Date: ‘Publié le 31 mai 2011 à 17h41’. Yield: none printed (6 used for scheduling). Times printed: ‘Préparation: 15 mn’, ‘Cuisson: 15 mn’. TWO-PASS, identical.
Cues in the original, short fragments: ‘la banane plantain doit prendre une belle couleur marron’; ‘si c’est tendre à l’intérieur, c’est cuit’. Slice thickness ‘1/2 à 1 cm’ — not converted.
ABSENT, not estimated: frying temperature, plantain ripeness, salt.
